source_refs.note: Topic 1.8.1, printed page 15, as printed: the reactions of sodium and magnesium with water and steam.

blocks.text: Sodium is more reactive than magnesium towards water. Na reacts vigorously with water to form sodium hydroxide and hydrogen while Mg reacts more slowly in forming magnesium hydroxide and hydrogen. However magnesium reacts with steam more vigorously to make magnesium oxide and hydrogen gas.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: This equation is not balanced: 4 H atoms and 2 O atoms on the left, 2 H and 1 O on the right. One molecule of steam reacts with each magnesium atom: Mg(s) + H₂O(g) → MgO(s) + H₂(g).
